function.name: bash
function.description: Execute one host shell command with the maintenance daemon's available permissions. Do not use sudo. Repairs are judged by actual file, process, and command effects; printing a claimed action or making only a backup does not repair the original. Exit code 0 means the command ran, not that the intended repair happened. The command parameter may instead be exactly one daemon control value: everything_ok (or yield), escalate uncertain MESSAGE, escalate unlocated MESSAGE, escalate no_fix MESSAGE, escalate temporary MESSAGE, escalate blocked MESSAGE, escalate failed MESSAGE, escalate rollback_failed MESSAGE, or escalate none ESCALATION_ID. Control commands may be called directly by name or through ~/.local/bin/<command>. A control value must be passed directly; never wrap it with echo, printf, bash -c, sudo, or another shell command.

command.description: An ordinary shell command that actually inspects or changes host state, or one exact daemon control value. A sed edit must include -i and the target file; sed without -i FILE only transforms input and does not edit. For manager systemd, restart the named service with systemctl restart SERVICE, never pkill it. A backup alone is not a repair, and echo without redirection only prints. Example control values: everything_ok; ~/.local/bin/escalate blocked operator credentials are required.
